# Correlated Erasure Capacity

This repository studies ordinary quantum communication through input-independent, flagged subset-erasure channels. Losses may be correlated within each finite block; blocks repeat independently. The sender has no realized-mask information, feedback, or preshared entanglement. Every elementary physical carrier is counted.

Start with README.md for the question and principal results, and science/README.md for the connected reading route.

## Authoritative routes

- Channel definition, complementary channel, stochastic flags, coherent information, regularization, and overlap converse: science/model.md.
- Exact additivity of the overlap-transport quantity and heterogeneous carrier dimensions: science/model.md.
- Uniform-local-survival minimum and supremum, imported Sun–Jafar codes, exact random-star capacities, binary share accounting, and exact marginal adjustment: science/capacity-envelope.md.
- Binary projective-plane code, complete one-qubit CSS stabilizer, line-local decoder, normal-vector flags, pairwise reduced-channel equality, and exact thinning capacity: science/geometry-and-loss.md.
- Inherited results, current source comparisons, and literature-version limits: references/related-work.md and references/references.bib.
- Reproduction commands, software dependencies, finite verification scope, and raw outputs: verification/README.md, verification/verify_geometry.py, and verification/results.json.

## Learning and reader routes

The single educational anchor is Nielsen and Chuang, Quantum Computation and Quantum Information, 10th Anniversary Edition (Cambridge University Press, 2010).

- Start self-directed study with learning/README.md. Use learning/anchor-and-bridge.md for the verified textbook sections, translated notation, and steps connecting the foundations to this project's results.
- Follow learning/milestones.md for exactly M01–M30, the project-defined background and scientific narrative. Each milestone supplies an understanding target, prior dependencies, conceptual connection, and scientific pointers.
- To understand the whole argument, read science/README.md, then model.md, capacity-envelope.md, and geometry-and-loss.md in science/.
- To inspect a theorem, use its authoritative topic page and references/related-work.md for the inherited ingredients and comparison scope.
- To reproduce a finite check, follow verification/README.md and distinguish a new execution from the recorded results.

The educational anchor supplies foundations. The regularized capacity theorem and the specific storage and geometric codes retain their primary research citations. The source bridge identifies the additional derivations supplied here. The milestone map is a common route through the scientific account.

## Essential distinctions

The capacity envelope is a supremum over finite block sizes and mask laws. The exact minimum is attained by independent erasure. The overlap quantity is a general upper bound, not an asserted capacity formula for every law. Additivity of that bound does not assert additivity of quantum capacity.

The geometric parameter q labels a finite field for the incidence structure; every physical site in those examples is still a single qubit. The separate Sun–Jafar construction uses larger shares, and all constituent qubits are charged.

Uniform line selection, uniform-normal-vector selection, and thinned line selection are different channels. The exact thinning formula belongs to the last one. Pairwise local-channel equality retains only the chosen local flags; the complete flag record distinguishes the correlations.

Use the topic pages for proofs and the references for attribution. The numerical checks cover stated finite cases and do not numerically determine general regularized quantum capacity.
